summary: With a global regular expression, match returns an array containing every full match in text order.
documentation: With a global regular expression, match returns an array containing every full match in text order. If there is no match it returns null. Global matching does not return capture-group details; matchAll is appropriate when those are needed.
returns: An array of ASCII ticket tokens.
caution: The pattern in this exercise finds tokens inside larger strings, including inside longer digit runs. It does not validate word boundaries or Unicode digits.
scenarios: Collect ticket references from support notes.
Extract known-format markers from a pasted log.
Build a local checklist of identifiers in a handoff document.
title: Extract ticket tokens
problem: Return every substring matching T- followed by exactly three ASCII digits, using non-overlapping left-to-right matches. For example T-1234 contains the match T-123. Return [] when none occur.
goal: Use String.match() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use /T-[0-9]{3}/g and replace a null match result with [].
